title: Why the iPhone Duo is already cracking

lines.text: Apple's *two-thousand-dollar* foldable iPhone has barely been out, and screens are already *cracking*.
To see why, you have to look *inside* the fold.
The inner screen isn't one sheet of glass. Apple says it's *ten* ultra-thin layers: a polymer cover, glass, the display itself, more glass, and a *titanium* plate.
Every time you close it, that stack bends into a tight curve. The outer layers have to travel *farther* than the inner ones, so Apple glues them with an adhesive that lets them *slide*.
Under all of that is the *hinge*. The repair experts at iFixit rebuilt it in 3D from *CT scans*, and they have three suspects.
Suspect one: the breaks cluster where a *gap* for a cable meets the hinge's central support. Several hard edges meet on one line, so every fold, the stress lands in the *same spot*.
Suspect two: curved rails that guide the fold may *lift* above the flat plates as it closes, and one of those rails lines up with the *damage*.
Suspect three is simpler. A speck of *dust* trapped in the fold, pressed into the screen every single time you close it.
Apple hasn't said which it is. iFixit even says some cracks might be a broken *connection*, not broken glass.
So if you just spent two grand on one, maybe close it *gently*. And send this to the friend who *pre-ordered*.
